summary: Backend-only regression for the seat-booking false-409 (drift) fix. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_seat_booking_reconcile.py with 9 tests across the exact scenarios requested. Full suite: 67/68 passing (all 59 pre-existing tests still green + 8/9 new). ONE new test failed — and it exposes a REAL secondary bug in the fix: the reconcile-and-retry logic only heals OVER-reporting drift (bogus/stale seats added to event.booked_seats). If drift instead UNDER-reports (a real seat is missing from event.booked_seats while a confirmed booking exists in the bookings collection), the atomic guard's first attempt SUCCEEDS (because the missing seat looks 'available'), reconcile-on-failure never fires, and the same seat is DOUBLE-BOOKED. I confirmed this by direct DB inspection: two separate confirmed bookings for seat E5 on the same event after the test ran. Between server restarts (which do a global reconcile) there is a real oversell window. Bug reported to main agent — see rca_of_issue.

critical.issue: Oversell / double-booking possible when event.booked_seats drifts to UNDER-report (i.e., loses a real seat entry while the booking still exists). Repro: (1) consumer A books E5 → 200. (2) directly modify event.booked_seats to remove E5 (simulate the drift class opposite to the one reported). (3) consumer B books E5 → server returns 200 and inserts a second confirmed booking for E5. Two confirmed bookings for the same seat now exist. Root cause: `_try_reserve` in _perform_booking only reconciles AFTER the first attempt fails; if drift REMOVES a taken seat, the first attempt SUCCEEDS and reconcile is skipped. The fix as designed only heals over-reporting drift (the reported user scenario) but not under-reporting drift. Fix suggestion: either (a) inside _try_reserve, cross-check the bookings collection for seat overlap on seat_map events BEFORE `$push`; or (b) always call _reconcile_event_availability(event_id) BEFORE the first _try_reserve; or (c) enforce a unique compound index on (event_id, seat) in a dedicated seat_reservations collection instead of an array on the event doc.

action_items: Fix under-report drift oversell in /app/backend/server.py::_perform_booking (see rca_of_issue). Preferred: call `_reconcile_event_availability(body.event_id)` unconditionally before the first `_try_reserve()` call for seat_map events, OR add a bookings-collection cross-check inside the atomic $push condition. Verify by rerunning test_drift_heal_still_rejects_real_conflict — it must return 409.
OPTIONAL long-term hardening: introduce a `seat_reservations` collection with a unique index on (event_id, seat_label) so the DB itself enforces uniqueness, eliminating any array-drift class of bugs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:433-464 `_reconcile_event_availability` is correct — rebuilds booked_seats/booked_slots/booked_count from the bookings collection (source of truth). Good.

server.py:467-487 self-heal on GET /api/events/{id}/booked-seats — verified working. Injected bogus ['BOGUS1','BOGUS2'] into event doc, hit the endpoint, and the doc was cleaned to []. Frontend view now matches truth.

server.py:559-568 reconcile-and-retry in _perform_booking — verified working for OVER-reporting drift. Injected ['ZZ99','F4','F8','A4','C5','F3'] into event.booked_seats with NO real bookings; first _try_reserve on 'F4' fails (F4 is in the array), reconcile clears it, retry succeeds. Good.

server.py:513-527 (seat_map _try_reserve) is the source of the under-report oversell: the $not/$elemMatch condition trusts event.booked_seats. If drift REMOVES a real seat, the check passes and $push adds a duplicate to the array with no cross-validation against the bookings collection.
server.py:1094 (startup reconcile-all) — good defense-in-depth for the reported bug class, but leaves an oversell window between restarts if the DB ever drifts to under-report.
server.py:590-600 rollback on `db.bookings.insert_one` failure is correct: pulls the seat back out of the array and decrements booked_count.
MongoDB _id exclusion is correctly applied throughout the seat/booking endpoints.

success_rate.backend: 67/68 (98.5%). All 59 pre-existing tests pass. 8/9 new tests pass; 1 new test exposes an under-report drift oversell bug (documented above).

All TEST_ events, their bookings, and test_seat_* users are deleted at end of the run (pymongo cleanup — see final block of test run). Demo users and prod-seeded events are not touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproducer for the newly-found HIGH-priority bug is TestDriftHealAndRetry::test_drift_heal_still_rejects_real_conflict in /app/backend/tests/test_seat_booking_reconcile.py — it injects drift by removing a real seat from event.booked_seats and asserts that a second consumer trying the same seat gets 409. Currently returns 200 (oversell). Once main agent applies the fix, rerun `pytest backend/tests/test_seat_booking_reconcile.py -v` — target 9/9 green. Note: BASE_URL comes from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env; MongoDB access from MONGO_URL + DB_NAME in /app/backend/.env. Cleanup pattern: delete events where title matches ^TEST_ and users where email matches ^test_seat_.
rca_of_issue:
REPORTED BUG (over-report drift): FIXED and verified. Bogus seats added to event.booked_seats (e.g. 'Y3d', 'F8', 'A4', 'F4' with no matching booking) caused the atomic guard to reject legitimate bookings. The fix reconciles from the bookings collection on guard failure and retries once — verified by test_drift_is_healed_on_booking_retry (injected ['ZZ99','F4','F8','A4','C5','F3'], no real bookings, then booking 'F4' returned 200). GET /api/events/{id}/booked-seats also self-heals — verified by test_get_booked_seats_self_heals_drift.

NEWLY DISCOVERED SECONDARY BUG (under-report drift → OVERSELL): The reconcile-and-retry code path only runs AFTER the first _try_reserve fails. If drift makes booked_seats miss a real seat, the first attempt SUCCEEDS (the seat looks free), so reconcile is never triggered, and $push happily inserts a duplicate. Direct DB check after the failing test shows two `confirmed` bookings with seats:['E5'] for the same event_id (two different user_ids). This means the same seat was sold twice — a real financial/customer-experience risk. Between server restarts (which do run the global reconcile), any process that mutates event.booked_seats incorrectly (bug, aborted transaction, out-of-order rollback) can open an oversell window until the next restart.

REPRO STEPS:
  1) POST /api/events (seat_map, 6x8, price=100) as demo@organizer.com.
  2) POST /api/bookings {event_id, seats:['E5']} as consumer A → 200.
  3) Direct DB write: db.events.update_one({id:event_id}, {'$set':{'booked_seats':['ZZ99','GARBAGE']}}).
  4) POST /api/bookings {event_id, seats:['E5']} as consumer B → 200 (BUG; should be 409). Verify db.bookings has two confirmed docs with seats:['E5'].

MITIGATION OPTIONS:
  (a) Call _reconcile_event_availability(body.event_id) BEFORE the first _try_reserve for seat_map (cheapest fix — one extra query per booking).
  (b) Add a bookings-collection cross-check inside _try_reserve (query for any confirmed booking overlapping requested seats; if any, treat as failure and go into reconcile+retry).
  (c) Long term: move seat reservations to a `seat_reservations` collection with unique index on (event_id, seat_label). Array-on-parent-doc is inherently drift-prone.
